articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of AppSys: An Online Appointment System
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: In the field of education today, communication between the teachers and the students are very much needed. Changes brought by the pandemic made consultations different as what people got used to during the traditional face to face consultations. Different problems arose including problems in scheduling and reaching the faculty members involved. An appointment system is made to manage appointments or bookings in a way that it could manage the schedule of the parties involved. This is done to optimize the schedule and properly set agendas, as well as the time of the parties involved. Using an appointment system, the students and faculties can communicate properly. National University uses Microsoft teams as a mode of communication during consultations. However, different studies found problems concerning the consultation happening in MS Teams including lack of time management and properly way of consultation from the students to the faculty. Through this system, a proper way of appointing schedule for out of the classroom consultation can be made. After testing the created system, the respondents were surveyed using the Technological Acceptance Model by Davis. The results showed an over-all mean of 4.55 from the student's perspective and 4.77 from the faculty's perspective.

articleTitle: Development and Application of E-Education Resources: Integrating PBL and FET to Improve the Teaching Quality of Mechanics Classroom
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: Problem-based learning (PBL) is gaining prominence as an effective student-centered pedagogy. However, traditional PBL implementations face challenges, particularly the lack of engaging digital course materials to stimulate problem discussions and conceptual understanding. This research proposes that high-quality E-education resources optimized for PBL could help address such limitations. In this study, finite element technology (FET) is leveraged to develop next-generation interactive E-learning content for PBL. FET simulations of engineering scenarios produce rich multimedia like colorful stress/strain nephograms and data visualizations. These digital resources are incorporated into existing PBL mechanics courses, seamlessly integrated with open-ended design problems. Experimental evaluation is conducted across four undergraduate classes, with quantitative and qualitative analysis of student engagement, learning outcomes, and satisfaction. Results demonstrate a 95.52% satisfaction rating with the innovative FET-powered e-resources. Significant improvements in PBL teaching quality are also observed. Overall, the findings validate FET as an effective approach for generating immersive PBL E-education materials. Its application illustrates how technology can transform PBL delivery and address longstanding challenges. Moving forward, continued exploration of synergies between technologies and forward-thinking pedagogies like PBL is warranted to advance education practices.

articleTitle: Perish or Prosper? The Challenges and Opportunities for Rural Micro and Small Enterprises in the COVID-19 Pandemic Crisis -The Role of E-Commerce
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: The raging COVID-19 pandemic in the past three years has had a great impact on people's health, life and work, as well as the business survival of enterprises and the overall social and economic stability. Rural MSEs are relatively short of capital and human resources, and it is more difficult for them to survive in the pandemic crisis. What difficulties and challenges did rural MSEs face during the pandemic? How did they respond and adapt? What role does E-commerce play in the survival of rural MSEs in the pande mic? These are the major questions this research seeks to understand. Qualitative research approach was applied to this study, in-depth interviews were conducted with semi-structured questionnaires, and content analysis was used to explore the possible answers to the research questions. It was found that during the most severe period of the pandemic, the most difficult challenges for agricultural MSEs in rural areas are: fearing that they and their employees will be infected and will affect their health and workforce (100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), followed by concerning that government control measures such as social distancing and movement restrictions will affect business operations and sales income (91.67<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), followed by worrying about whether the cooperative logistics distributors can deliver online shopping goods to consumers as smoothly as before(75%). The coping actions taken by rural agricultural MSEs during the pandemic include: setting employee health management and work rules, conducting more sales activities on electronic platforms, developing new products based on customers' feedback. According to the findings, this study suggests that rural agricultural MSEs can make good use of electronic platforms to expand customer base, manage online customer relationships, promote high quality products during a crisis like COVID-19 pandemic. By doing so, MSEs can improve their E-business operation capabilities and accumulate better crisis resilience for the future.

articleTitle: E-Learning Methods and Tools for Effective Teaching in Networking and Cybersecurity Courses
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: This paper presents various methods and tools for effectively teaching the concepts in data communications, networking, and cybersecurity. The topics may be covered in one or two senior undergraduate course(s) or one first year graduate CS course. Methods of effective E-Learning, including blended and cooperative learning are discussed and applied in the design of these courses. The covered topics range from basic concepts of data communications to some of the advanced cybersecurity concepts now considered as one of the core CS areas.

articleTitle: Identification Assessment of Applying Artificial Intelligence Image Generation Techniques in University Computer Graphics Courses
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: Drawing has always been a fundamental course in design education at the college and university level. With the advancement of technology, various emerging technologies have been introduced into teaching practices. In recent years, there has been significant attention given to the application of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, which has garnered admiration for its ability to produce remarkable images. This study aims to introduce new AI techniques for providing guidance and suggestions in drawing, with the goal of addressing the issues present in traditional computer graphics instruction. The study seeks to examine whether the new technology is capable of improving students' learning outcomes and fostering their interest in the subject. Data was collected through questionnaires administered to 52 game design students aged between 17 and 22 years old. Prior to the questionnaire survey, the students received instruction in computer drawing using AI image generation technology. Independent sample t-tests were conducted to investigate the relationships between gender, prior experience with AI image generation technology, and various variables. However, no statistically significant correlations were observed. Additionally, exploratory factor analysis identified two correlated constructs: satisfaction and applicability.

articleTitle: The Usability Testing of Website with Automated Tools (A Case Study at School of Information Systems, BINUS University)
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: The Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) field has grown significantly over the past few decades. Websites are now crucial tools for the distribution of digital material. In order to compete worldwide and give everyone the information they need. Therefore, websites need to be usable and accessible. The usability of a website is related to how simple it is to use, while accessibility is required for successful and efficient web use. The author uses the School of Information Systems website as an object for this research. This research will concentrate on using an automated tool to assess websites. The research objectives are to examine the usability and performance of the website, including information delivery methods and the utilization of every aspect the website offers visitors. The research uses automated tools to evaluate websites such as WAVE, Tenon, Google Lighthouse, and Pingdom. The results of this research could assist stakeholders in improving the quality of the website in order to boost user satisfaction and experience.

articleTitle: Integrative Narratology and Its Application in AI-based Virtual Education System
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: Narratology is a scientific study of narrative. The primary functions of narrative are make sense of life and make present life experience. Narrative has permeated our lives since ancient times as powerful tools to express and communicate human thoughts, emotions, creativity and for understanding the world. The pervasive nature of narrative extends beyond personal experiences. It has the potential to enhance quality of life, foster social progress, and human civilization. The 21st century is an era of digital narrative. Narrative form and structure have undergone tremendous changes. Most of the narrative theories of the 20th century are no longer applicable. To integrate the diverse range of narratives types in the 21st century and seamlessly fuse them with artificial intelligence (AI) and the metaverse technologies, this paper announces a bland new narrative discipline named “Integrative Narratology”. To develop this new discipline, this article proposes an integrated narrative conceptual framework and construct an integrated narrative system(INS) based on this framework. In addition to describing this framework, its theoretical foundations, core technologies and INS, this article also briefly introduces the method of AI automatic story generation, as well as how to use INS to automatically generate stories. How can we teach students to learn how to adapt to the social change caused by the rapid advancement of AI and metaverse technologies? Policy innovation and education reform are urgent tasks. Therefore, this article proposes an AI-based virtual education system based on INS for innovation in education technology. The evolution of AI technology, its application in metaverse, and the metaverse technologies applicable to this education system are described. The development of this virtual education system and its learning models are illustrated. Finally, the modern AI apocalypse and the conclusion are summarized.

articleTitle: Collaborative Learning and Self-Regulation: The Mediating Role of Self-Efficacy
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: Self-regulated learning is vital for empowering students to take charge of their learning and actively manage their academic efforts. However, second language learners often struggle with self-regulation, indicating a need for support in developing self-regulation strategies. This study aimed to explore the interplay among collaborative learning, self-efficacy, and self-regulation in a blended learning English course, utilizing an online survey questionnaire completed by 91 undergraduate students. Three multiple regression analyses were conducted to scrutinize the mediating role of self-efficacy in the relationship between collaborative learning and self-regulation. The mediating effect was further validated by a bootstrapping method, which demonstrated that self-efficacy partially mediated the relationship. These results have important implications for educators, highlighting the need to create effective collaborative learning experiences that foster self-regulation skills in second language learners.

articleTitle: Breaking Barriers: Designing Digital Inclusion and Digital Literacy Learning Programs for Senior Citizens
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: This article discusses an approach to promoting digital inclusion among senior citizens in Malaysia through intergenerational learning program. This program is an initiative and collaborative effort between a public and private university, as well as industry experts. It involves teaching older adults on digital creativity and literacy through learning modules presented in a face-to-face format with mentoring partnerships between younger and older individuals. The modules were developed based on the preferred learning strategies of older adults and local cultural context. From the standpoint of the European Digital Competence Framework for Citizens, this article outlined the methodology used to create the digital inclusion and digital literacy learning programs and attempts to explore how the digital learning program is aligned to the competences featured in the framework by comparing the learning outcomes from each learning module against the competence descriptions for each competence area. The potential improvements to the program and the implications of promoting this initiative are also discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Coupling and Coordination of Regional Digital Economy and Innovation Ability under the New Development Pattern
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: The paper constructs the evaluation index of digital economy development level and regional innovation ability from multiple angles and dimensions. Based on the panel data of 30 provinces and cities in mainland China from 2011 to 2020, the entropy method is used to determine the weight of the index. The linear weighting method is used to assess the digital economy development level and regional innovation ability of provinces and cities. The coupling coordination degree data of each province is obtained through the coupling coordination degree model. The research results show that the development level of the digital economy and the development trend of regional innovation ability in most provinces and cities are good, but the regional development difference is significant. In view of the development index and coupling status of the two, the paper proposes some policy recommendations, such as optimizing resource allocation, adjusting macro policies, and strengthening regional cooperation.

articleTitle: Explaining Instructional Factors Affecting M-Leaming Using the Moderator of Social Media: An Extension of the IS and TAM Models
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: Information and communication technology (ICT) is a term which refers to the incorporation of electronic technologies to manage knowledge and information. It has transformed the traditional education system into an efficient and flexible e-learning context. E-learning enables the higher-education institutions to create a traditional-like virtual classroom. The universities must stay abreast with the current technology to evaluate the quality factors that affect the e-learning process. This paper presents a theoretical study of the quality factors affecting e-learning in the mobile environment and presents two research contributions. First, we propose a model which suggests to add social media as a moderator that effects the relationship between user's satisfaction and user's intention-to-use. Second, we propose to add instruction quality attribute to the existing variables of well-recognized TAM and Extended IS models which enhance the e-learning experience within the mobile environment in higher education institutions in Saudi Arabia.

articleTitle: Enhancing Physics Education with Collaborative Learning through Computerised Experiments
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: It is evident from the reality that society's survival and progress rely on cooperation. When communities work together to tackle common tasks, they unlock the power to solve problems that would be impossible for individuals alone. In this context, the abilities and contributions of each member become crucial for achieving success. Thus, fostering the capacity for Collaborative Learning (CL) has become an essential skill for every individual in the modern era [1]. Consequently, the development of CL skills among students has become a prevalent educational trend worldwide. This study presents the following research findings: the implementation of a teaching approach that incorporates both real and computerised experiments to facilitate CL among students; the design and utilisation of experiments in the ‘Electromagnetic Induction’ lesson and the extracurricular lesson ‘Designing a Simple Generator - Applying the Phenomenon of Electromagnetic Induction’ in 11th-grade Physics classes, aimed at creating an environment for CL; and the demonstration of how experiments can be employed to enhance students' CL abilities through the ‘Magnetic Induction’ lesson at Thuan Hoa High School, Hue City, Vietnam. Additionally, we conducted pedagogical experiments during the 2022–2023 academic year to assess the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing students' CL capabilities. Based on the CC of CL competence and the CL competence assessment table developed, each evaluation criterion is divided into 4 levels including Level 1 (low level); Level 2 (intermediate level); Level 3 (decent level); Level 4 (advanced level), we do pedagogical experiments to assess the development of CL competence of students in lessons. The results of the assessment of CL competence after applying the teaching process using experiments in the lessons in the chapter ‘Electromagnetic Induction’ (Physics 11) showed that the number of students who scored CL competence at level 3 and level 4 in the later stage (phase 2) are more than in the first stage (phase 1) in the experimental process pedagogy. This has confirmed the feasibility of using experiments in teaching Physics to develop CL for students, thereby improving the effectiveness of teaching Physics in high schools. articleTitle: Who are More Satisfied with Online Learning: Students who have prior Exposure to Face-to-Face Learning or Students who have none?
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on E-Society, E-Education and E-Technology (ESET)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has drastically changed the education landscape in the Philippines. From traditional face-to-face Learning, the Philippines suddenly shifted to online learning to help curb the transmission of the COVID-19 virus. However, due to limited preparations, studies have shown drawbacks in the education system, particularly in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs). After more than a year of online learning implementation, the study seeks to determine the student's preparedness and satisfaction with online learning and how their exposure to Face-to-Face instruction influences it before going entirely online. Through convenience sampling, 1221 respondents were obtained from National University - Philippines and its two campuses, National University (NU MoA) and National University (NU Laguna). The results revealed that the top three (3) constructs with the highest agreement with online Learning were Authentic Learning, Instructor Support, and Student Autonomy. Differentiating students with and without exposure to Face-to-Face show a statistically significant difference in terms of Collaboration, Adequate Technology, and Online learning Satisfaction. While the results show that learners are reasonably satisfied with Online Learning, the study shows that those without F2F learning exposure before going online had a higher perception of online learning satisfaction than those with exposure to F2F. Regarding readiness, the data reveal that students with F2F exposure had less preparation for adequate technology
